paper_core_claims.claim: A closed well-typed FPC expression either diverges or deterministically yields a unique value.
Concurrent FPC preserves types but deliberately does not guarantee determinism, deadlock freedom or progress.
RCF uses refinements, assumptions and assertions so that a well-typed expression satisfies the paper's semantic assertion-safety property.
F7 implements a practical approximation of RCF for F#/Objective Caml, erases refinements for ordinary runtime execution, and sends logical obligations to Z3.
Refinement contracts can encode authenticity, session causality, audit-evidence correctness/completeness and stateful access-control obligations.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A function is a typed lambda-calculus value whose dependent refinement type carries logical preconditions and postconditions. Type checking composes these contracts with assumptions, channel refinements and solver deductions, producing an ordinary executable after refinements are erased.
representation_or_carrier: The formal carriers are FPC/Concurrent-FPC/RCF expressions, values, dependent refinement types, logical formulas, typing environments, assumed-formula logs, typed channels, structures and proof obligations. The paper also derives channel pairs, mutable references and a refined state monad as encodings. These are symbolic program carriers, not learned weights or probabilistic functions.
specification_language: RCF admits value-dependent refinements {x:T|C}, dependent functions and pairs, assume/assert formulas and typed channels over a parameter logic with basic closure properties. Preconditions and postconditions can mention values and protocol predicates. Expressiveness and decidability depend on the chosen logic, prover, axioms and subtyping discipline; the source does not define resource, privacy, deployment, ownership or lifecycle contracts.
compiler_or_generator: The formal checker extracts formulas from typing environments, reduces refinement subtyping to logical deduction and enforces assertion obligations. F7 adds partial inference, polymorphism, controlled subtyping and algebraic datatypes, sends nontrivial first-order obligations to Z3, and emits plain F# interfaces by erasing refinements. A separate session compiler is described as generating protocol code plus detailed refinements for F7 verification, but its implementation is not packaged here.
interpreter_or_runtime: FPC has deterministic call-by-value reduction; Concurrent FPC/RCF adds asynchronous messages, fresh names, fork, nondeterministic scheduling and possible deadlock. Assumptions update a logical log for the safety model and assertions reduce without runtime enforcement. F7 refinements are erased, so ordinary F#/Objective Caml runtime behavior and cryptographic libraries remain outside the static checker unless modeled by trusted contracts.
composition_rule: Dependent application substitutes argument values into result refinements; channel types transfer asserted facts across message boundaries; fork typing exchanges active assumptions; and the refined state monad composes pre/post-state predicates. This is a formal contract-flow discipline. It neither supplies arbitrary effect isolation nor proves that separately written specifications are mutually complete or semantically compatible.
state_or_effect_model: Concurrent FPC directly models threads, channels, message stores, name generation, nondeterminism and deadlock, and can encode mutable references. RCF adds a global assumption log and assertion observations; the refined state monad describes permission-state transitions. Exceptions, timing, resource consumption, probabilistic effects, Byzantine implementation faults, lifecycle changes and real network cryptography are not fully operationalized by the core calculus.
uncertainty_model: Judgments and logical deductions are categorical within the selected formal model; there is no calibrated probability or confidence. Conservative rejection can occur for safe but untypable programs, and proof success is conditional on trusted assumptions, axioms, library contracts and prover behavior. Application summaries report no repeated trials, confidence intervals or independent replication, so they are qualitative evidence rather than uncertainty estimates.

equivalence_notions.boundary: For concurrency this does not imply progress, determinism or deadlock freedom.
This is relative to the logic and admitted assumptions and does not assert liveness or full functional correctness.
Decidability is conditional on an oracle for formula derivability.
Erasure preserves base typing, not runtime monitoring or provenance.
Both depend on the judge and evidence contracts being faithful to the intended property.

lifecycle_and_provenance: The PDF records report identity, a December 2010 correction, publication history, named F7 version and citations. It does not pin F7, Z3, F#/OCaml, library, protocol, compiler or case-study revisions; publish hashes or verification receipts; define compatibility migrations; or model approval, monitoring, revalidation, rollback, supersession and retirement. Refinement results can become stale when code, interfaces, axioms, solvers or trusted cryptographic libraries change.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The exact atlas metadata was wrong: the source is by Gordon and Fournet, not Vazou, and is a 2009 technical report with a December 2010 corrected version, not a 2016 work.
FPC type safety permits divergence, and Concurrent FPC additionally permits nondeterminism and deadlock; preservation is not total correctness or liveness.
RCF assumes formulas may be introduced with assume; the authors explicitly say program assumptions should be carefully reviewed.
Assertions have no runtime checking effect in the calculus, and F7 erases refinements before normal execution.
The safety theorem covers assertion entailment in the modeled calculus, not arbitrary exceptions, resource use, timing, privacy, availability or real cryptographic implementation defects.
Logical strength and decidability depend on the chosen logic, axioms and prover; conservative typing rejects some semantically safe programs.
The theorem presentation is tutorial-level: several proofs are sketched or exercises and complete proofs are delegated to a cited report.
The security applications rely on trusted typed libraries and contracts and are summarized from related projects rather than independently evaluated here.
F7 and all application artifacts lack immutable revisions and a durable verification-result manifest in this PDF.
Categorical SAFE/typable judgments are not empirical confidence and do not establish the completeness of the specification.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not prove deadlock freedom, liveness, termination or complete functional correctness for concurrent programs.
It does not make arbitrary assumptions, axioms, cryptographic libraries or specifications trustworthy.
It does not supply runtime refinement enforcement, probabilistic uncertainty or end-to-end artifact lifecycle governance.
It does not independently reproduce every cited security application or validate the complete Function OS architecture.

corrections: Replaced the atlas's incorrect Vazou/2016 metadata with Gordon/Fournet and the 2009 report plus December 2010 corrected-version identity.
Separated FPC progress from Concurrent FPC preservation and recorded nondeterminism/deadlock as explicit boundaries.
Distinguished semantic assertion safety, trusted assumptions, refinement erasure and application-level cryptographic contracts.
Recorded the tutorial proof boundary, lack of pinned F7/application artifacts, categorical uncertainty and lifecycle gaps.

confirmed_projection: The tutorial gives direct formal and implementation-descriptive support for a dependent FunctionSpec, symbolic Representation, solver-backed Compiler, refinement-erased Artifact, explicit concurrent Interpreter semantics, Validator and contract-flow Composer. Execution receipts, probabilistic uncertainty and VersionedRegistry lifecycle remain partial.
source_specific_reasoning: CONFIRMED is warranted for the bounded architectural pattern: the paper builds three calculi from first principles, distinguishes preservation/progress/safety, defines dependent refinements and formula flow, states the RCF safety theorem, describes the F7/Z3 checker and connects it to several security patterns. The status is not a claim of complete proof or empirical reproduction: many proofs are exercises or delegated, applications are summaries, assumptions and library contracts are trusted, concurrency can deadlock, and refinements are erased at runtime.
projection_boundary: These are 121CX projections from the exact hash-matched 35-page corrected Microsoft Research report and primary Microsoft publication metadata. Formal statements apply within the paper's calculi; implementation and application descriptions were not independently rerun. This is not proof of the complete Function OS, real-world security, liveness, specification completeness or final truth freeze.
